checked.found: Hammurabi's accession is 1792 BC in the middle chronology (other chronologies differ by decades); description is supported and gives no date.
Nabopolassar took the Babylonian throne in 626 BC, founding the Neo-Babylonian dynasty; name and description are fine.
Alexander crossed the Hellespont and won at the Granicus in 334 BC; name and description are fine.

Arsaces I is dated from 247 BC as the first Parthian king; Wikipedia notes the seizure of Astabene around 238 BC as the nominal start of the Arsacid era, so a minor source split exists, but 247 BC is the conventional date.
Modu killed his father Touman and took power in 209 BC (traditional date resting on Xu Guang); description is supported.
